slice_results.behavior_summary: When called, the code modifies HTML image tags in input content by parsing and appending explicit width and height attributes with pixel or percentage units, using string manipulation and regular expressions. It accesses and modifies string data representing HTML content but does not perform any network, file, system, or cryptographic operations. This behavior purely transforms input data for presentation purposes without involving sensitive API calls or suspicious data.
slice_results.explanation: [LLM Judgment: Benign] The provided code purely performs string manipulation and HTML content transformation by parsing tags and appending width and height attributes with pixel or percentage units. It does not perform any file system, network, cryptographic, or dynamic code execution operations. Compared to the known malicious patterns, it lacks any form of payload extraction, dynamic eval or Function execution, obfuscation, or injection of executable code. The behavior is consistent with a benign plugin designed to enhance image tag presentation in HTML content. There are no suspicious API calls or patterns that indicate malicious intent.

matched_snippet.code_behavior: During postinstall, the code reads image files (logo1.jpg, logo2.jpg, logo3.jpg), extracts ASCII payloads from their byte data, and if a threshold is met, dynamically executes the extracted string as JavaScript code, resulting in arbitrary code execution sourced from image-embedded payloads.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Extracting and executing code from image files is a classic steganography-based evasion technique, designed to bypass static analysis and conceal malicious payloads within seemingly benign files.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages do not extract and execute code from image files during installation, nor do they use dynamic code execution on data sourced from non-code files.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate image processing libraries may read and analyze image files, but never execute dynamically extracted code from image data.
key_indicators: Steganographic payload extraction from image files
Dynamic code execution using new Function() on extracted strings
Threshold-based trigger for code execution (payload length > 2000)
References to analyzepixels, convertertree, and imagebyte variables

package_info.why_malicious: The package is a trojanized clone of a legitimate library, containing concealed code that, during installation, extracts and executes a command-and-control (C2) payload hidden within image files. This enables remote code execution and exfiltration of command results, granting attackers persistent remote access to infected systems.

attack_chain.action: During installation, index.js spawns a detached process to execute dist/loadformat.js.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of the malicious loader script in a separate process.

attack_chain.action: dist/loadformat.js reads image files (logo1.jpg, logo2.jpg, logo3.jpg), extracts ASCII payloads, and dynamically executes code if a threshold is met.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of the C2 payload if present in the image files.

attack_chain.action: Extracted C2 payload registers the client with the attacker's server, polls for commands, executes them, and exfiltrates results.
attack_chain.leads_to: Full remote control of the infected system and exfiltration of command output.

behavioral_signatures: Postinstall script spawns detached Node.js processes using spawn/unref
Image files (logo1.jpg, logo2.jpg, logo3.jpg) are read and parsed for ASCII payloads during installation
Dynamic code execution via new Function() on data extracted from image files
Outbound HTTPS connections to hardcoded IP address 85.208.108.29 for registration, polling, and result exfiltration
Periodic polling for remote commands and execution of arbitrary shell commands
file_indicators: index.js containing spawn/unref logic targeting dist/loadformat.js
logo1.jpg, logo2.jpg, logo3.jpg in package root directory
References to analyzepixels, convertertree, and imagebyte variables in code
network_indicators: Outbound POST requests to /register and /post-result endpoints
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for npm packages that, during installation, spawn detached Node.js processes, read and parse image files for ASCII payloads, or dynamically execute code extracted from non-code files. Flag packages making outbound connections to hardcoded or suspicious IPs (e.g., 85.208.108.29) or exhibiting periodic polling for remote commands. Scan package contents for the presence of suspicious image files (logo1.jpg, logo2.jpg, logo3.jpg) and loader scripts (dist/loadformat.js), and inspect for code patterns involving analyzepixels, convertertree, and imagebyte.

matched_snippet.code_behavior: At runtime, the code decodes hex-encoded payloads using hexilify(), then executes the decoded JavaScript using eval(), enabling dynamic execution of hidden malicious logic that can perform further data collection or exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Use of eval() on dynamically decoded hex strings is a classic obfuscation and code injection technique, allowing attackers to hide and execute arbitrary payloads at runtime.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages rarely, if ever, use eval() on decoded hex data, as this is a hallmark of obfuscated malware.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some obfuscation libraries may use similar techniques, but not in open-source packages or for legitimate runtime logic.

execution_context.file_location: hexilify() and eval() usage in main code files

package_info.why_malicious: The RED-LILI campaign distributed hundreds of npm packages, including 'wf_ajax', containing highly obfuscated and evasive malicious code. These packages exfiltrate sensitive data, evade sandbox analysis, and establish persistence on victim systems. Tactics include executing code from files masquerading as documentation, embedding payloads in non-code files, anti-analysis logic, and spawning background processes to maintain access and continue data theft.

attack_chain.action: Malicious package is installed, triggering the preinstall script that executes code from a documentation file.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of obfuscated payload hidden in README.md

attack_chain.action: Obfuscated code in README.md or index.js is executed, performing anti-analysis checks to determine if the environment is a sandbox or automated scanner.
attack_chain.leads_to: Conditional execution of main malicious payload if not in analysis environment

attack_chain.action: If anti-analysis checks pass, the main payload is decoded from hex and executed using eval(), enabling further malicious actions.
attack_chain.leads_to: Data collection and exfiltration logic is activated

attack_chain.action: A detached background process is spawned to run bgService.js, maintaining persistence and enabling ongoing malicious activity.
attack_chain.leads_to: Continued data exfiltration or further attacks after installation

attack_chain.action: Collected data is exfiltrated to attacker-controlled domains via outbound HTTP/S requests.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives sensitive data from compromised systems

behavioral_signatures: Execution of README.md or other documentation files as code during npm install
Presence of obfuscated JavaScript payloads in non-standard files (e.g., README.md)
Use of eval() on dynamically decoded hex strings at runtime
Preinstall scripts that spawn detached child processes (e.g., bgService.js)
Anti-analysis logic such as UUID/hostname checks to evade sandboxes
file_indicators: lib/README.md or README.md containing obfuscated JavaScript code
package.json with preinstall script referencing documentation files (e.g., 'node lib/README.md')
Presence of bgService.js or similarly named background service files in package directory
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/S connections to domains such as *.fuzzdb.cf, *.pipedream.net, *.requestbin.net, *.33mail.ga, *.22timer.ga
Network activity initiated during or immediately after npm package installation
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor npm package installations for preinstall scripts that execute non-standard files, especially documentation files like README.md. Flag packages containing obfuscated JavaScript in documentation or non-code files. Detect use of eval() on decoded hex strings at runtime. Alert on packages that spawn detached child processes during install. Monitor for outbound network connections to known RED-LILI campaign domains or webhook services during or immediately after package installation.

matched_snippet.code_behavior: During content creation or editing, the code injects an tag with a javascript: URL in the src attribute, which is stored in the Drupal database and rendered in the page body, potentially triggering JavaScript execution in the victim's browser if not properly sanitized.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The use of a javascript: URL in the src attribute is a classic XSS vector, allowing arbitrary script execution if not blocked by sanitization.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal sanitization should strip or block javascript: URLs in image src attributes to prevent script execution.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: There is no legitimate use for javascript: URLs in image src attributes; images should reference valid image resources.
key_indicators: Presence of javascript: scheme in src or data-cke-saved-src attribute
Bypassing of URL scheme sanitization in image tags
Execution of JavaScript via image loading

execution_context.trigger: During content creation or editing, and at runtime rendering of content
execution_context.file_location: CKEditor instance in Drupal content editor (client-side), content stored in Drupal database, rendered in page body
required_permissions: Ability to create or edit content
Potential network access if XSS payload is used for exfiltration

package_info.why_malicious: Multiple cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerabilities in the FigCaption widget and widget handling allow attackers to inject arbitrary HTML, attributes, and classes into user-generated content. These flaws bypass expected sanitization, enabling stored and self-XSS, page defacement, and user redirection. The vulnerabilities break HTML sandboxing and can be exploited by low-privileged users to execute malicious scripts in the context of other users.

attack_chain.action: Attacker crafts and submits malicious HTML payloads using FigCaption or widget attributes, such as arbitrary classes, javascript: URLs, or <script> tags, via the content editor.
attack_chain.leads_to: Payload is stored in the Drupal content database as part of user-generated content.

attack_chain.action: Stored payload is rendered in the CKEditor instance or on the public-facing page, causing the browser to process and execute the injected HTML, attributes, or scripts.
attack_chain.leads_to: XSS, page defacement, or user redirection occurs as the malicious content is executed in the victim's browser.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code executes in the victim's browser, enabling actions such as session hijacking, user redirection to attacker-controlled domains, or exfiltration of sensitive data.
attack_chain.leads_to: Account compromise, phishing, or further exploitation of the victim's session or data.

behavioral_signatures: User-generated content containing <script> tags or javascript: URLs in HTML attributes
Presence of overlay classes such as joyride-modal-bg in user content
Arbitrary data-* attributes or non-whitelisted classes in <figcaption> or widget HTML
Image tags with src or data-cke-saved-src attributes using the javascript: scheme
file_indicators: Content fields in the Drupal database containing <script> tags, javascript: URLs, or suspicious overlay class names
Unusual or non-whitelisted attributes in
Presence of data-cke-* attributes with unexpected values in stored content
network_indicators: Unexpected outbound HTTP or HTTPS requests triggered by user interaction with rendered content (e.g., redirection to external domains such as attacker.com)
JavaScript execution resulting in network requests to attacker-controlled domains or IP addresses
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan user-generated content in the Drupal database and rendered pages for <script> tags, javascript: URLs in HTML attributes, and suspicious classes or data-* attributes in figcaption and widget HTML. Monitor for DOM elements with overlay classes or non-whitelisted attributes. Use web application firewalls (WAFs) to block known XSS payloads and monitor for suspicious outbound network activity originating from user interaction with content, such as redirections or JavaScript-initiated requests to external domains.

matched_snippet.code_behavior: At content render-time during widget rehydration, the code parses the data-cke-widget-data JSON and sets the src attribute of the tag to a javascript: URL, resulting in potential execution of arbitrary JavaScript in the user's browser.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Permitting widget data to set critical attributes like src without validating the URL scheme allows attackers to inject javascript: URLs, leading to XSS.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Widget data should be sanitized and only allow safe URL schemes (e.g., http, https). Here, the widget logic trusts unsanitized user input, enabling execution of malicious code.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use of data-* attributes is for storing widget state, not for setting executable code or dangerous URL schemes.
key_indicators: data-cke-widget-data JSON with src set to javascript: URLs
img tags with src or data-cke-saved-src attributes containing javascript: schemes
Widget rehydration logic that applies unsanitized user input to DOM

execution_context.trigger: content render-time (widget rehydration in editor or page view)
execution_context.file_location: CKEditor widget HTML, with data-* attributes

package_info.why_malicious: Drupal Core contains multiple cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerabilities in the FigCaption widget and widget handling logic. These vulnerabilities allow attackers to inject arbitrary HTML, attributes, and classes into content, leading to account hijacking, web content injection, page defacement, and redirection attacks. The root cause is inconsistent sanitization between client-side and server-side code, and insufficient attribute whitelisting, which enables malicious payloads to bypass security controls.

attack_chain.action: Attacker crafts and injects malicious HTML payloads using FigCaption or widget attributes, such as script tags, overlay classes, or javascript: URLs.
attack_chain.leads_to: Payload is stored in Drupal content or previewed in the CKEditor editor.

attack_chain.action: Payload is rendered in the CKEditor preview or on the Drupal site, triggering DOM manipulation, script execution, or UI overlay.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is executed in the victim's browser, or the page is defaced or redirected.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code executes in the victim's browser, enabling account hijacking, phishing, or further exploitation.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains control over user sessions or exfiltrates sensitive data.

behavioral_signatures: Presence of <script> tags or javascript: URLs in data-caption or widget data attributes
Use of overlay or UI-manipulating classes (e.g., 'joyride-modal-bg') in captions or widget HTML
Injection of arbitrary attributes or data-* attributes in FigCaption or widget HTML that affect rendering or behavior
file_indicators: Drupal node HTML content containing or tags in captions with suspicious attributes
data-caption attributes containing HTML elements or script tags
data-cke-widget-data JSON with src or href fields set to javascript: URLs
network_indicators: Unexpected redirections to external domains (e.g., https://attacker.com) from Drupal content
Outbound HTTP requests initiated by injected JavaScript during user sessions
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan Drupal content fields and CKEditor widget data for suspicious HTML, such as <script> tags, javascript: URLs, or overlay classes in captions. Monitor for unexpected redirections or DOM changes during page render. Use web application firewalls (WAFs) to block script injection and enforce strict attribute whitelisting in FigCaption and widget logic. Implement automated scanning for data-caption and data-cke-widget-data attributes containing executable code or non-whitelisted classes.

matched_snippet.code_behavior: During user input in source mode, the code injects a <script> tag into the data-caption attribute, which is rendered in preview mode, resulting in the execution of arbitrary JavaScript and triggering a browser alert.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The injection of <script> tags into user-editable fields without proper sanitization enables execution of arbitrary JavaScript, which is a critical XSS vulnerability.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior should sanitize or escape script tags in captions to prevent script execution. Here, the preview mode fails to sanitize input, allowing direct execution of user-supplied scripts.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: There is no legitimate use case for allowing script tags in image captions; captions should only contain safe, sanitized text or basic formatting.
key_indicators: Presence of <script> tags in data-caption attributes
Execution of JavaScript in CKEditor preview mode
Lack of sanitization on user-supplied HTML in captions

execution_context.file_location: CKEditor instance in Drupal content editor (FigCaption widget, client-side)
